key_headlines.summary: Second quarter nominal GDP surged 26.4% year-over-year, the highest rate in 47 years, driven by semiconductor export price increases. Bank of Korea warns of inflation and financial imbalance risks amid this exceptional growth.

key_headlines.title: Young Adults Embrace Stock and Bond Investments for Retirement Planning
key_headlines.summary: The proportion of people in their 20s and 30s using stocks and bonds for retirement planning increased fivefold over 14 years, reaching 12.8% and 13.4% respectively. Post-retail investor boom sustains two-digit participation.

key_headlines.title: Seoul 59-Sqm Apartment Average Asking Price Nears 1.6 Billion Won
key_headlines.summary: August average sale price for Seoul's 59-square-meter apartments reached 1.593 billion won, approaching the 1.6 billion mark. Prices in semiconductor belt areas like Dongtan surged 17.5% year-over-year.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea's economy shows exceptional nominal growth of 26.4% in Q2, driven by soaring semiconductor export prices, but the Bank of Korea warns of mounting inflation and financial imbalance risks. The youth employment crisis persists with 28 consecutive months of decline in August, prompting government intervention with a proposed 90,000+ job recovery plan. Concurrently, Korean battery makers are losing competitive ground to Chinese competitors outside China, with North American supply down 43%. Meanwhile, young adults increasingly embrace equity and bond investments for retirement planning, with participation rising fivefold over 14 years. Seoul apartment prices continue climbing near 1.6 billion won for standard 59-square-meter units.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Korean economy's nominal GDP growth reached 21.8-26.4% in the first half of 2026, marking the highest rate in 47 years, primarily driven by improved semiconductor export prices and better terms of trade. The Bank of Korea expressed concerns about demand-side inflation pressures and potential financial imbalances as rapid nominal growth could fuel asset price expectations and household leverage expansion. Policy officials including Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced plans for advancing steel industry modernization in Q4, focusing on AI manufacturing innovation, high-value specialty steel, and hydrogen-based steel reduction. Rising government revenue from nominal GDP expansion may ease fiscal pressure, though concerns persist about household debt acceleration and widening credit imbalances in financial markets.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean won-dollar exchange rate remained anchored around 1,330 won despite triple headwinds of rising oil prices, higher US Treasury yields, and declining stock markets, defying typical correlation patterns. The KOSPI struggled to maintain the 7,000-level benchmark amid the quadruple pressure of elevated US bond yields, AI bond demand, rising Japanese interest rates, and surging crude oil prices approaching 100 dollars per barrel. Market observers attributed the won's resilience to complex dynamics where higher US rates paradoxically failed to strengthen the dollar. As the Federal Reserve's September FOMC meeting approaches, market participants await employment and inflation data to assess whether rate hikes will continue or pause. Global long-term interest rates remain stubbornly elevated, creating persistent upward pressure on Korean financial markets.
sections.Industry & Technology: Korean semiconductor companies face intensifying competition from Chinese chipmakers, prompting calls for coordinated national strategy beyond individual corporate investment decisions. Hyundai Motor and Kia partnered with LG Energy Solution to launch pilot projects recycling used EV batteries into energy storage systems, leveraging their E-GMP platform and linking charging infrastructure. Global experts identified defense and nuclear power as promising next growth sectors for Korea, with analysts highlighting that nations exceeding 3% global growth rates typically enjoy growth premiums. Current policy rate differentials between the US and Korea are supporting won strength despite recent weakness, creating opportunities for Korean tech exports and inbound capital flows.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's 59-square-meter apartment average sale price reached 1.593 billion won in August, approaching the 1.6 billion mark with 1.97% monthly increase, while Incheon saw prices rise 7.02% to 539 million won. The semiconductor belt region, particularly Dongtan in Gyeonggi Province, experienced exceptional 17.5% year-over-year appreciation as housing demand surged near major chip manufacturer facilities. Financial authorities warned of mounting financial stability risks as household debt continues accelerating, concentrated in the capital region where housing prices show persistent strength. Gangnam's three districts (Seocho, Gangnam, Songpa) weakened as high-property tax concerns prompted adjustments, while other Seoul areas and premium large complexes near transit hubs remain supported. Property market divergence reflects policy uncertainty regarding tax amendments targeting high-value residences and non-primary homes.
sections.International Economy: A prominent economist who criticized Trump's tariff policies faced rejection for IMF chief economist appointment, highlighting political tensions over protectionism versus multilateral cooperation. Trump administration tariffs are expected to persist even after administration changes, with supply chain reconfiguration presenting opportunities amid US-China tensions over excess Chinese production. US copper imports surged to record 22.5 million tons in July as importers rushed purchases ahead of anticipated Trump tariffs, with copper prices climbing on dual AI demand and protectionism fears. The Federal Reserve faces narrowing options as oil prices breach 100 dollars per barrel, US Treasury yields surge, and inflation concerns mount despite weak employment data, creating uncertainty for rate decisions at mid-September FOMC meetings. Global commodity and credit markets face compounding pressures from fiscal deficits, AI infrastructure buildout, and mounting geopolitical tensions.
sections.AI & Economy: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries announced over 1 trillion won investment in land-based power generation engines and small modular reactors to capture AI data center power demand opportunities. The company will construct a new HiMSEN engine production facility in Ulsan with 3GW capacity and a dedicated SMR manufacturing plant, targeting 2028 completion with combined annual output reaching 4GW. TSMC's August revenue surged 53% year-over-year as semiconductor equipment demand more than doubled since year-end, with production capacity roughly quadrupled yet still unable to meet explosive AI infrastructure demand. Industry observers project chip equipment manufacturers will source from ASML at 400 million dollars per unit from 2030 onward as AI infrastructure investments accelerate globally. Power generation and nuclear technology represent emerging strategic sectors as AI data centers consume unprecedented electricity volumes.
sections.Others: Single-stock leveraged ETFs requiring regulatory framework adjustments after breaching negative divergence rate thresholds within 72 days of listing, highlighting financial product stability concerns.
